exposure: Maternal subclinical hypothyroidism in first trimester
Maternal isolated maternal hypothyroxinemia in first trimester
Maternal subclinical hypothyroidism in third trimester
Maternal isolated maternal hypothyroxinemia in third trimester
cohort: The study included 52,027 pregnant women in Shanghai who underwent first-trimester antenatal screening, with 34,860 included in the final analysis after having both first and third trimester thyroid function data.
finding: The impact of maternal mild hypothyroidism (subclinical hypothyroidism and isolated maternal hypothyroxinemia) on obstetric and perinatal outcomes varies significantly depending on the trimester of pregnancy, with third-trimester subclinical hypothyroidism and first/third-trimester isolated maternal hypothyroxinemia generally associated with adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: Isolated maternal hypothyroxinemia in the first trimester was associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery.
birth_weight: Outcomes measured include large for gestational age, small for gestational age, and macrosomia.
gest_age: Outcomes measured include preterm birth, large for gestational age, and small for gestational age; exposures were assessed during specific gestational age windows (first trimester: 8-14 weeks, third trimester: 30-35 weeks).
